fix(start-wrt): answer plain HTTP at the public address with a redirect to HTTPS while 443 is published (#4000)

* fix(start-wrt): redirect plain HTTP at the WAN address to HTTPS while 443 is published

StartOS asks its IPv4 gateway for no port-80 mapping: it publishes only 443
and expects the gateway to answer plain HTTP at the public address with a
redirect to HTTPS, as StartTunnel does. StartWRT never implemented its half,
so a LAN client opening http://sub.example.com for a domain pointing at the
WAN address hairpinned to the router's own port 80 and got the router UI.

Port control now binds a listener to <WAN IPv4>:80 beside the daemon's
wildcard :80 (both SO_REUSEPORT; the kernel delivers a connection to the
most specific socket) and hands each connection to start-core's shared
handle_http_on_https, a 307 to the same host and path over HTTPS. The socket
is never wired into the axum app, so it can serve nothing but the redirect,
and the LAN gateway addresses and router.lan still reach the UI.

No firewall rule is touched: who may reach WAN:80 remains the Remote Access
policy; this changes only what answers there. The listener is bound only
while WAN 443 leaves the router (an enabled WAN DNAT covering tcp/443, or a
live hostname route on 443) and yields to a DNAT on tcp/80, so a router
publishing nothing on 443 behaves exactly as before. Reconciled at port
control startup, on the sweep, on hostname route changes, and when a manual
published port is saved.

* fix(start-wrt): admit WAN-side HTTP to the port-80 redirect through a DNAT

The redirect listener on WAN:80 answered only connections the wan zone
already admitted, so under Remote Access "Never" (or "When behind NAT"
with a public address) a client on the Internet opening
http://sub.example.com was refused. StartOS publishes only 443 and leaves
port 80 to its gateway, and that half of the contract was unmet from
outside.

An ACCEPT on wan tcp/80 would be fail-open: UCI rules persist across a
daemon restart and fw4 loads them before the daemon binds, so the UI's
wildcard :80 socket would answer in that window or after a failed bind.
Instead, port control writes a wan-zone DNAT (`startwrt_http_redirect`,
no dest_ip, which fw4 renders as an nft `redirect to :8880`) while 443 is
published, and the redirect binds 0.0.0.0:8880 beside its WAN:80 socket.
fw4 accepts DNAT'd connections at input, so no ACCEPT rule opens 80, and
with the daemon down the DNAT lands on a closed port.

The section carries its own marker option rather than `_apf_label`,
which the sweep would lease and collect and the UI would list as an
automatic forward. `wan_dnat_covers` ignores it so the redirect does not
gate itself off, `apply_forward_uci` still counts it so PCP/UPnP grants
for external 80 conflict while it is active, and `sni_port_conflicts`
reserves 8880 so no hostname route can out-rank the wildcard socket. The
section's presence no longer depends on knowing the WAN address, which
avoids a remove-and-re-add firewall reload at every boot; only the WAN:80
hairpin socket needs the address.

Reconciliation runs under `write_serial`. Callers that already hold it
use the serialized variant, and `published_ports::set` skips the
redirect's own firewall reload since it reloads anyway. A settled section
is never rewritten, so the sweep does not reload fw4 every minute.

Under "Never", port 80 now answers a 307 instead of rejecting while 443
is published. It echoes the requested Host and can serve nothing else.

* refactor(start-wrt,core): decide the port-80 redirect in the request path

The redirect bound two sockets of its own — <WAN>:80 for LAN hairpins and
0.0.0.0:8880 behind a wan-zone tcp/80 DNAT for the Internet side — because a
socket bound after the UI's wildcard :80 cannot be admitted by an ACCEPT rule
without the UI answering in the gap between the two binds. Deciding per
request removes the gap and with it the reason for both sockets: an outermost
layer on the router answers a request whose destination is the WAN address
with a 307 and passes everything else through, live from the first accepted
connection. StartOS makes the same trade in net/domain_redirect.rs.

Gone with them: port 8880 and its reservation, the hairpin rebind on every WAN
renumber, the startwrt_http_redirect section and its marker, the family field
on FirewallRedirect, the impostor-replacement logic, and wan_dnat_covers'
exclusion of its own section.

The Internet side is now a WAN ACCEPT rule on tcp/80, carried in the SNI
admission set rather than reconciled separately, so sync_sni_rules is the one
place the redirect is decided. It keeps the SNI label deliberately: a label
older builds do not know is a rule older builds never purge, and such a rule
outliving a downgrade would admit plain HTTP to a daemon with no layer behind
it. Sharing the label means a rollback purges it on its first run, as it
already does for a stale apf_sni_443.

The gate the layer reads is that rule's presence, not "443 is published". The
two disagree exactly at startup — a hostname route does not survive a restart
but the rule it earned does — so the gate is seeded from UCI before the
listener binds and tracks what the firewall actually admits. Until port
control resolves the WAN address the layer redirects rather than falling
through, since a double-NAT WAN is not separable from the LAN by address
class.

TcpMetadata.local_addr now comes from the accepted stream rather than the
listener, which is the connection's destination on a wildcard socket and
identical to the old value on a specifically bound one. served_name and
arrival are its only readers and both want the destination.

Also reserves port 80 against hostname routes while the redirect is up, which
the DNAT did not: a UPnP grant could take external 80 and be silently dead
WAN-side.

* fix(start-wrt): serve the UI on port 80 by client subnet, not by destination alone

The port-80 admission rule matches the wan zone, not a destination, and the
layer redirected only a request whose destination was the WAN address. Four
consequences, found auditing b700399fb against the PR discussion:

A WAN-side host that routes the LAN subnet through the router's WAN address
arrives at the LAN address and was served the plaintext UI under "Never". The
DNAT this replaced caught all wan-zone tcp/80, so that was a regression. The
layer now serves the UI only to a client on a subnet the router is connected
to off the WAN, at an address that is not the WAN's; every other IPv4 request
gets the 307. The gate carries every WAN address rather than the first.

After a restart the gate was seeded admitted with no WAN address, which
redirected every plain-HTTP request, LAN included, until the first 60 s sweep
and for as long as the WAN had no address. Addresses are now read before the
listener binds, when port control starts, on every sweep and WAN hotplug, and
once more (at most every 5 s) before a redirect is answered, so a bridge that
comes up after the daemon is trusted on its first request. With the WAN down
there is no WAN subnet to exclude and the LAN keeps the UI.

The gate was set to the wanted state before the rule was reconciled, so
unpublishing 443 shut it while fw4 still admitted WAN:80 — the UI answered
there until the reload finished, or indefinitely if it failed. It now opens
before the rule is written and shuts only after the reload that removes it.

A hostname route on 80 writes the same section under the same label, and the
redirect's rule was identified by port alone: the route's own rule read as
the redirect's, so its renewal was refused as taken and a manual port-80
forward was refused rather than displacing it. The rule's name now tells the
two apart, the redirect yields to a live route on 80, and the rule is
rewritten when the port changes hands. The seed still opens the gate on any
SNI rule on 80, since a lapsed route's rule admits the same traffic. The
label stays shared, so a build without the redirect still purges the rule.

Not migrated: the startwrt_http_redirect section written by 720777534. It
reads as a user's port-80 forward and holds the redirect off, but no build on
master ever wrote it; a bench router that ran that commit needs
`uci delete firewall.startwrt_http_redirect`.

* docs(start-wrt,core): cut the port-80 redirect comments and docs to the facts

Review on #3999 asked for the mannered prose to go throughout, and this branch
carried the same habits: a 23-line module doc, doc comments that argued their
rationale and named their callers, tests narrating what their names state, and
user docs saying the same thing three times.

Each comment is now one fact. The changelog entry, release note,
`published-ports.md` and `settings.md` state the behavior once.

`ARCHITECTURE.md` also described the layer as keyed on the connection's
destination, stale since 3f1fa0d38, and omitted the per-request reread of stale
addresses.

Comment-only in every `.rs` file.

* fix(start-wrt): answer a Host-less request on WAN:80 with 400, never the UI

`redirect()` returned `None` when the request carried no usable `Host`, and
`respond()` read that as "not the redirect's request" and fell through to the
UI. A WAN-side client could reach the plaintext router UI while 443 is
published with `printf 'GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n' | nc <WAN> 80`, under every
Remote Access setting.

Once the layer has decided a request redirects, it now always answers: a 307
with an authority, a `400 Host header required` without one, which is what the
standalone redirect socket this layer replaced answered.

* fix(start-wrt): admit WAN tcp/80 for the redirect at the WAN address alone

The redirect's admission rule matched the wan zone with no destination, so
the firewall also admitted a WAN-side packet for the router's LAN address to
the daemon, and only the layer's client-subnet check kept it from the UI. The
rule now carries `dest_ip` set to the WAN address, so such a packet is
rejected at the firewall as it was before the redirect existed; the layer's
check stays as the second line.

Port control rewrites the rule when the WAN address changes (the sweep and
the WAN hotplug already invalidate the cached address) and writes none while
the address is unknown. The gate still opens whenever the redirect is wanted,
so a LAN hairpin to the WAN address redirects with or without the rule.

* fix(start-wrt): seed the port-80 gate before port control can raise it

`port_control::run` was spawned before `http_redirect::seed` ran. `run`
raises the gate before writing the admission rule; `seed` sets the gate
to whether an SNI rule on 80 is already on disk. On the first boot of a
router that already publishes 443, no such rule exists yet, so `seed`'s
parse could read the old firewall and its `set_admitted(false)` land
after `run`'s `set_admitted(true)`: rule live, gate shut, listener
bound, and WAN:80 served the plaintext UI until the first sweep at 60 s.

Seeding before the spawn leaves "rule absent, gate shut" as the worst
boot state, which the firewall refuses.

Found by helix-nine in review of #4000.

* fix(start-wrt): a ubus failure leaves no client trusted on port 80

`wan_ipv4_addrs` returns an empty list on a ubus failure, which the gate
could not tell from a WAN with no address. With no WAN address to
subtract, the WAN interface's own subnet stayed in the trusted set, so a
peer on that subnet dialling `<WAN>:80` got the UI instead of a 307
while the admission rule was still live from a cached lookup, until the
next successful read.

`read_wan_ipv4_addrs` returns `None` on a ubus failure and the gate then
trusts no subnet; an empty list still means the WAN is down and keeps
serving the LAN at its own address.

fix(start-wrt): ship the fw4 include files where sysupgrade replaces them (#4101)

StartWRT staged its nftables includes into /etc/nftables.d/, which firewall4
lists in keep.d. A sysupgrade restores the old router's copies over the new
image's, so a changed file stays at its old version and a removed one stays
loaded. No release has changed or removed one yet.

/etc/nftables.d/ is the user's include directory. Stock OpenWrt keeps it
whole and never merges it. Package-owned includes belong in
/usr/share/nftables.d/, which is part of the image. The files now go in
/usr/share/nftables.d/table-pre/, which fw4 includes at the same point in
`table inet fw4`, so every sysupgrade installs the image's copies.

A uci-defaults script deletes the copies earlier images left in
/etc/nftables.d/, by exact name. It runs from /etc/init.d/boot (START=10)
before the firewall starts (START=19). Without it fw4 loads both copies and
merges each chain, running every rule twice.
